subject: Part 5 spt_dur_sleep_min low for Cole Kripke with Neishabouri Counts results in low sleep_efficiency

messages.author: e5b9e6a13d6fc253
messages.subject: Part 5 spt_dur_sleep_min low for Cole Kripke with Neishabouri Counts results in low sleep_efficiency
parts:
Hi Vincent and Jairo,

We are working on a comparison analysis running the HASIB.algo = "ColeKripke1992" with do.NeishabouriCounts = TRUE using the HASPT.algo = "HDCZA" on some ActiGraph .gt3x files. We've observed relatively low spt_dur_sleep_min in part 5 resulting in lower than expected sleep efficiency.

As a check of these data we also re-ran it with HASIB.algo = "VanHees2015" and HASPT.algo = "HDCZA" and we get much more plausible spt_dur_sleep_min and subsequently sleep efficiency. This is also observed for the case with the counts using the ZC method on the Cole Kripke data. 

We are running GGIR 3.1.0 on R 4.4.0 using the nonwear_approach = "2023".

I have attached a comparison of the config files from the two examples and a subset of the part 5 output for one individual to demonstrate. 

Is the low spt_dur_sleep_min using Cole Kripke and Neishabouri counts expected? We ran it in ActiLife also and obtained sleep efficiency results closer to the VanHees2015 and ZC Cole Kripke method when setting the bounds of the sleep period to be the same. 

Thanks,

Sam

parts:
Hi Samuel,

Cole Kripke did not design their algorithm for Neishabouri counts, so it is not surprising that it does not work.

See also my response to: https://groups.google.com/g/rpackageggir/c/kxZ1RjWCmBs/m/dMQ0Vj4HAgAJ

The documentation I refer to in that message has been moved to https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/chapter4_AccMetrics.html#notes-on-implementation-of-zero-crossing-counts

Thanks,

Vincent
